You were installing an entirely new desktop environment on top of the existing one.

Did you tell your .xinitrc file to use the new DE?

The .xinitrc file is a text file in your home folder. It tells your system what DE you prefer to be loaded. New DEs like to screw with it. You need to open it up in an editor and unfuck it. The must be only one uncommented DE.

Apparently for ElementaryOS the actual DE is called Pantheon. In order to run it the line you need in your .xinitrcis exec cerbere Does that make sense? Nope, neither do I.

Also apparently several things need to happen correctly before exec cerbereis run, so putting it on its own in .xinitrc won't work, you need other stuff before it. Read here if you are brave. Beware that this describes a very different system, you don't have neither pacman nor AUR on Mint so nothing in the installation section would work, but in theory if you can find all the corresponding packages in your own repositories the rest should work the same.

I strongly advise you to get familiar with the use of man pages.

man is a command which retrieves the documentation for a command at the terminal. Before you run a new command, say "foo -uP dog", look up the command and its parameters by typing "man foo"
